title: Remote Psychotherapy for Caregivers of People with Dementia
summary:
Of the 1.8 million people with dementia in Germany, 86% are cared for primarily by family members at home (Federal Institute for Population Research, 2025). Family members thus form the backbone of dementia care. This home-based care presents a wide range of challenges: Family caregivers not only assist with routine tasks but also frequently have to deal with strong emotional reactions, such as restlessness or anxiety, on the part of those affected. At the same time, they are confronted with their own feelings of grief and worry due to the gradual loss of shared experiences. As a result, family caregivers often have little time to attend to their own needs and interests or to find a balance in their lives. It is not uncommon for family members of people with dementia to report symptoms of exhaustion, depression, and anxiety, which have a serious impact on their health and quality of life.
As part of the study, psychotherapeutic counseling sessions are offered to family caregivers of people with dementia, either by phone or video call. Topics covered in the sessions may include, for example, understanding changes caused by the disease, coping with grief, symptoms of depression and anxiety, exhaustion, worries, rumination, and feelings of guilt, as well as building a support network and incorporating self-care activities into daily life. The sessions are conducted by trained psychotherapists, specializing in behavioral therapy. To ensure that any positive changes can be attributed to the psychotherapeutic sessions, family caregivers are randomly assigned to either an intervention group or a control group. Both groups receive comprehensive written information on various caregiving-related topics, but only the caregivers in the intervention group receive psychotherapeutic support sessions. Both groups are asked to complete questionnaires on various topics at four different time points over a 12-month period—including depressive symptoms, other stress-related symptoms, resources, physical complaints, and quality of life.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Adult caring relative of a person aged 60 or older with diagnosed dementia who is currently being cared for at home and will continue to be so in the foreseeable future (at least 3 months) (no plans to move to a nursing home).
- The care and support must average at least 1.5 hours per day or at least 10 hours per week (including travel time).
- Access to a telephone or internet connection.
- Significant stress related to caregiving reported during the screening interview (two out of three criteria from a brief screening: caregiving-related physical or mental health problems, loneliness, caregiver burden).
Exclusion criteria:
- Acute, severe mental illness or ongoing psychotherapy of the participating caregiver
- Participation in another intervention study for domestic caregivers
- Insufficient knowledge of German
- Hearing or vision problems that would make it difficult to conduct telephone interviews or complete questionnaires
